newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: South African shares ended 1996 in a firm mood as buoyant international markets and the unit trust close-out gave prices a lift, dealers said on Tuesday.

They said positive sentiment from recent record highs in London and New York was still supporting South African stocks and also pointed to a degree of price manipulation as unit trusts sought to boost their books before the end of the year.
"There was some selective demand for stocks. It is mostly due to the unit trust-close-out," one dealer said.
The final session of the year ended early at noon (1000GMT) as traders prepared for New Year's Eve festivities, but volumes were a healthy 218 million rands worth of shares.
The all-share index closed at 6,657.5, up 29.1 points, as industrials ticked up 34.7 points to 7,921.6.
Dealers said the rise was likely to continue when trade resumes on Thursday. "The trend at the moment is upward. The market is still a little cheap," one dealer said.

Performance among blue-chips was mixed with De Beers dropping 25 cents to 134.00 rand and SA Breweries shedding 50 cents to 118.50 rand while Anglos put on 150 cents to 257.50 rand and Minorco added 25 cents to 98.25 rand.
The gold market was quiet as the bullion price rose a fraction in early European trade. But most gold shares rose as dealers foresaw a break through the psychologically important $370 an ounce level.
The golds index firmed 5.4 points to 1,506.2.
The futures market had another quiet day and also ended trade early. Futures opened slightly firmer in thin business hovering near Monday's settlement levels, but slipped slightly at the end.
The all-share March contract was at 6,155/65 from 6,227 and the industrials contract stood at 7,670/705 from 7,735. The golds contract ticked to 1,055/65 from 1,064.
